description: A pregnant Nigerian traveller is assessed against an assumption about why she is travelling, regardless of her actual purpose - which makes a visa harder and a border harder at exactly the point in life when travel is least comfortable.
energy_note: Interrogated at a border while visibly pregnant.

description: Nigerian-trained doctors and nurses face examinations, supervised practice and language testing before working at their level - years in which they work below their training and are paid accordingly.
energy_note: A consultant, working as a junior, for three years.

aspect: And the accent is assessed as competence
description: Patients and colleagues read a Nigerian accent as a proxy for training quality. The clinician learns to speak differently, which is unpaid work performed during a shift.
energy_note: Flattening your own voice, for eight hours a day.

aspect: SCENARIO - the nurse who is 'not yet' a nurse
description: Fourteen years on a Lagos ward. In the UK she is a healthcare assistant for nineteen months while her registration proceeds, doing much of the same work, at a third of the pay, being trained by people she has more experience than.
energy_note: Fourteen years of experience, re-entered at the bottom.
